activity.notes: Harald Fairhair (Old Norse Haraldr hárfagri; Norwegian Harald Hårfagre) is treated by current Norwegian reference historiography as an early Norwegian king, probably ruling from around 865 until roughly 930-933. Later medieval narratives made him the sole conqueror and unifier of all Norway, but modern scholarship regards the unification as a much longer process and debates the geographical extent of Harald's actual authority. ATLAS therefore reuses Kingdom of Norway as the representative polity while recording 865-930 only as an approximate reign window, not as exact accession/death dates or as proof that he exercised uniform control over the territory of modern Norway. His best-supported power base lay in south-western Norway and along the coastal sailing route.

sources.title: Harald Hårfagre — Store norske leksikon
sources.citation_text: Store norske leksikon states that Harald Hårfagre was king in Norway from around 865 until his death around 930-933, while stressing that the later image of him as sole unifier of all Norway is debated and that his core power lay in south-western Norway and control of the coastal route.

sources.title: The Beginning of the Viking Age in the West — Journal of Maritime Archaeology
sources.citation_text: The article discusses Harald Fairhair as a ruler who rose to power around the Rogaland-Hordaland sailing route and extended control along the Norðvegr, supporting a regional and route-based interpretation of his kingship rather than a simplistic instantaneous unification narrative.
